# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260926-1305-acrelec-validation`
- Research system: `ChatGPT Deep Research`
- Started at: `2026-09-26 13:05 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-26 13:07 CDT`
- Research scope: Direct-competitor customer-page mining
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:acrelec`
- Methodology: Four first-party Acrelec customer case studies were opened and assessed. Vendor-authored results remain attributed claims and were not written into canonical records.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 0
- Conflicts found: 1
- Material takeaway: Acrelec has named, product-specific self-service deployments at BIM'S, Steak 'n Shake, Jollibee UK, and Dunkin U.S. The pages show credible kiosk hardware, ordering software, POS, loyalty, and cash-automation integration depth, but three sources describe 2021-era deployments and none establishes a current 2026 global estate.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: BIM'S
- Vendor: Acrelec; Glory
- Product or category: K27 self-service kiosk; CI-Hybrid 15 cash automation; payment and loyalty scanning
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: location-level
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Acrelec's dated first-party case study names BIM'S and its managing director, identifies the products, and describes the second London restaurant deployment.
- Source title: Passion for Customer Service: BIM'S Installs Joint Kiosk & Cash Self-Service Solution
- Source URL: https://acrelec.com/casestudies/passion-for-customer-service-bims-installs-joint-kiosk-cash-self-service-solution/
- Publisher or source owner: Acrelec
- Published date, if known: 2023-06-08
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The case study says BIM'S installed Acrelec's K27 kiosk integrated with Glory's CI-Hybrid 15 payment station when opening its second restaurant; the named executive reports 25% more sales through self-service than the counter till.
- Product-specific evidence: K27 self-ordering, CI-Hybrid 15 cash handling, card and mobile-wallet payments, barcode-scanner loyalty support, and cash/card payment choice.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: This is a vendor-authored result from one newly opened location; it does not establish deployment across a larger BIM'S estate or continued use in 2026.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm the current BIM'S location count, live kiosk estate, and software/POS integration.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Steak 'n Shake
- Vendor: Acrelec
- Product or category: DOT15 and planned K22 PRO self-ordering kiosks; DOT19 application; Aloha and Glory CI integration
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: historical
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: Acrelec's dated first-party case study explicitly names Steak 'n Shake inside the deployment narrative and reports observed pilot and rollout counts.
- Source title: Cooking up self-service for America's leading steakburger restaurant
- Source URL: https://acrelec.com/casestudies/cooking-up-self-service-for-americas-leading-steakburger-restaurant/
- Publisher or source owner: Acrelec
- Published date, if known: 2021-10-28
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Acrelec reports a DOT15 pilot at select Steak 'n Shake locations, deployment at more than 60 locations, and a plan to install K22 PRO kiosks at 500 stores by the end of 2021.
- Product-specific evidence: Self-ordering hardware and UI, real-time Aloha POS communication, Glory CI cash-management integration, upsell and limited-time-offer logic, loyalty and scanning features, and ADA-oriented interaction design.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page shifts from DOT15 pilot hardware to a planned K22 PRO rollout and future DOT19 application. The 500-store figure is a 2021 plan, not proof of completed rollout or current 2026 use.
- Recommended follow-up: Locate a current Steak 'n Shake technology source confirming live kiosk count and which Acrelec hardware/software generation remains deployed.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Jollibee
- Vendor: Acrelec
- Product or category: K27 self-ordering kiosks; DOT XIX software; NCR/Aloha POS integration
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Acrelec's dated first-party case study names Jollibee, the UK pilot, installed kiosk and location counts, and specific software and POS integrations.
- Source title: Upselling the joy of chicken with Jollibee
- Source URL: https://acrelec.com/casestudies/upselling-the-joy-of-chicken-with-jollibee/
- Publisher or source owner: Acrelec
- Published date, if known: 2021-09-23
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Acrelec reports that a Leicester Square pilot was followed by 17 additional K27 kiosks at four UK locations by the end of June 2021.
- Product-specific evidence: K27 hardware, DOT XIX UI and ordering software, Barclays EFT reader, personalized upsells and limited-time offers, NCR/Aloha real-time POS integration, and dine-in/takeaway modes.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is UK-scoped and historical. Five additional sites, 15-20 more sites, a drive-thru, content management, digital menu boards, and Philippines expansion were plans under discussion, not completed deployments.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm the current UK estate and whether Acrelec expanded beyond the original UK deployment.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Dunkin'
- Vendor: Acrelec
- Product or category: K27 self-ordering kiosks; DOT XIX software; Simphony POS, gift-card, and loyalty integration
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Acrelec's first-party PDF names Dunkin', specific products and integrations, and a measured U.S. rollout count through May 2021.
- Source title: Customized kiosk solution increases throughput
- Source URL: https://acrelec.com/wp-content/themes/themeacrelec/assetsv3/landingdunkin/Acrelec_CAESTUDY_dunkin_intranet.pdf
- Publisher or source owner: Acrelec
- Published date, if known: 2021
- Accessed date: 2026-09-26
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The case study says a custom K27 pilot at one busy U.S. store expanded to more than 320 kiosks at over 235 locations through the end of May 2021.
- Product-specific evidence: K27 hardware with camera and EFT-reader modules, DOT XIX UI, Simphony POS integration, gift cards, loyalty, upsell options, and ADA-oriented interaction design.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The source is historical and U.S.-scoped; the reported 17% average-check lift is vendor-authored and the page does not establish current 2026 use or a systemwide Dunkin' deployment.
- Recommended follow-up: Verify current live location and kiosk counts and whether the Simphony, loyalty, and gift-card integrations remain active.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: Acrelec's named QSR relationships establish current 2026 global, enterprise-wide deployments.
- Pages checked: All four pages in the source ledger.
- Result: Unsupported. BIM'S is location-level; Jollibee is a four-location UK rollout; Dunkin' is a historical partial U.S. rollout; Steak 'n Shake mixes completed 2021 counts with planned expansion.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://acrelec.com/casestudies/passion-for-customer-service-bims-installs-joint-kiosk-cash-self-service-solution/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 1 | Productive; named K27 plus Glory cash-automation deployment. |
| https://acrelec.com/casestudies/cooking-up-self-service-for-americas-leading-steakburger-restaurant/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 2 | Productive historical rollout; planned figures kept separate from completed deployment. |
| https://acrelec.com/casestudies/upselling-the-joy-of-chicken-with-jollibee/ | case study | 2026-09-26 | 3 | Productive UK deployment evidence with NCR/Aloha integration. |
| https://acrelec.com/wp-content/themes/themeacrelec/assetsv3/landingdunkin/Acrelec_CAESTUDY_dunkin_intranet.pdf | case study | 2026-09-26 | 4 | Productive historical U.S. deployment evidence with Simphony, loyalty, and gift-card integration. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Acrelec's competitive strength is end-to-end customization across kiosk hardware, ordering UI, POS, loyalty, payments, and cash automation. This packet does not establish that Acrelec supplies the core POS itself.
- Inference: The strongest visible large-chain proof in this batch is historical and regionally scoped, so current-estate verification should precede any 2026 competitive installed-base claim.
